notes.claim: Dan's course flowchart is headed "Electrical Circuit Design Calculation Process" for BS 7671:2018 + Amd2:2022, and its note 2 separates a suitable protective conductor size from the minimum protective conductor size.
The showroom supply is three phase four wire 400 V, TN-C-S, with Ze declared as 0.1 ohm and a prospective fault current of 4.6 kA; the ambient temperature is 20 degrees Celsius.
The showroom adds a 400 V three-phase 11 kW motor at power factor 0.8 lagging and efficiency 86%, controlled by a star-delta starter.
Overload protection is the condition Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz (Regulation 433.1.1), plus I2 ≤ 1.45 Iz, where I2 is the current causing effective operation of the protective device.
The course slides take √3 as 1.73, so their printed answers can differ in the last decimal places from the same sum worked with the calculator's √3.

sources.title: Requirements for Protection Against Overload - Professional Electrician
sources.quote: The rated current or current setting of the protective device (In) should not be less than the design current (Ib) of the circuit.

sources.title: Requirements for Protection Against Overload - Professional Electrician
sources.quote: The current (I2) causing effective operation of the protective device should not exceed 1.45 times the lowest current-carrying capacity (Iz) of any of the conductors of the circuit.
